title: Longest Palindromic Substring
contract: Return the longest palindromic substring, choosing the leftmost on ties. Empty input returns an empty string.
brute: String best="";for(int l=0;l<s.length();l++)for(int r=l;r<s.length();r++){boolean ok=true;for(int i=l,j=r;i<j;i++,j--)if(s.charAt(i)!=s.charAt(j)){ok=false;break;}if(ok&&r-l+1>best.length())best=s.substring(l,r+1);emit("Test an interval","range",new int[]{l,r},"best",best);}return best;
optimal: int start=0,length=0;for(int center=0;center<s.length();center++)for(int parity=0;parity<2;parity++){int l=center,r=center+parity;while(l>=0&&r<s.length()&&s.charAt(l)==s.charAt(r)){if(r-l+1>length||(r-l+1==length&&l<start)){start=l;length=r-l+1;}emit("Expand around an odd or even center","range",new int[]{l,r},"best",s.substring(start,start+length));l--;r++;}}return s.substring(start,start+length);
reasoning: Enumerate each interval and compare mirrored characters.
Every palindrome has one character center or one gap center. Expand while the two sides match.
This improves the cubic baseline to quadratic time with constant auxiliary space. Manacher's algorithm can reach linear time; center expansion is the simpler optimized interview solution shown here.
